bullets.title: Fed turns hawkish under Warsh: 9 of 18 FOMC dots expect 2026 rate hike
bullets.body: The June FOMC meeting delivered a hawkish surprise with 9 of 18 participants projecting at least one 2026 rate hike (6 expecting two or more), core PCE forecast revised sharply higher to 3.3% for 2026 (from 2.7% in March), and Chair Warsh dropping forward guidance and shortening the statement. Markets re-priced to ~36-40bp of hikes through year-end. Fed's reaction function now centers on monthly core PCE: ~0.21% monthly keeps the Fed on hold; recent readings tracking ~0.36% keep tightening live. Morgan Stanley sees Fed on hold through year-end; JPMorgan calls first hike in H2'27 as base case but margin for error is limited.

bullets.title: US-Iran deal reopens Hormuz: oil slides 10%+, inflation tail risk collapses
bullets.body: A US-Iran MOU signed Friday allowed immediate Iranian oil exports and reopened the Strait of Hormuz; WTI fell ~10% on the week to the mid-$70s, gasoline dropped below $4/gallon for the first time since March. ~80M barrels on 21 supertankers were ready to transit immediately. Wolfe estimates the deal could add 4+ million barrels/day of supply by 2027, and long-dated WTI signals more durable headwinds. 2-year breakeven inflation dropped to 2.19% from a 3.37% March peak, and oil tail risk pricing was cut by ~75%.

bullets.title: Lower oil + hawkish Fed creates bifurcated playbook: favor tech/discretionary, avoid energy
bullets.body: Multiple strategists converge on the same macro trade: benign growth deceleration toward ~2% with falling oil prices supports early cyclicals (tech, discretionary, communications) which carry the highest equity duration and benefit most from lower yields. At the same time, energy stocks face a structural supply headwind from the Iran deal, and the Fed's tightening bias is most damaging for rate-sensitive small caps and non-AI cyclicals. Citi prefers Banks, Materials, QQQ, and AI power generation. 22V and JPMorgan both flag tech/discretionary as the clearest beneficiaries.

bullets.title: Record US equity inflows ($119B week of 6/17) and S&P 500 up 11 of past 12 weeks
bullets.body: US equity inflows hit a record $119.2B in the week ended June 17, tracking toward $739B for full-year 2026 if pace holds. The S&P 500 was up for the 11th week out of the past 12, within ~1.5% of its all-time high. Semis led with the SOX up 113% YTD — more 5%+ momentum moves in 2026 than the prior 8 years combined. Dow and Russell 2000 hit fresh record highs during the week. Retail demand was concentrated in TSLA, NVDA, MU, MSFT, and SNDK.

bullets.title: AI capex supercycle revised up to $5.5T through 2030; MSFT faces $90-130B funding gap
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised total AI infrastructure capex estimates to $5.5T through 2030 (from $5.1T), with 138GW of data center capacity as the base case and 85%+ LTC debt financing. Google and Amazon are aggressively pre-funding FY27-28 capex (~$300B each per year), while Microsoft is ~1 year behind with an estimated $90-130B FY27-28 funding gap — making it the most likely source of sizable new IG supply in 2H26. FERC unanimously approved Trump's plan to accelerate data center grid connections. OpenAI's $600B stated capex plan looks stress-tested at only ~$300-500B supportable given ~39% gross margins.

bullets.title: Semis positioning extreme: 32% of HF gross leverage, SMH +113% YTD, VaR shock risk flagged
bullets.body: Hedge fund semiconductor exposures more than doubled YTD to record highs (32% of gross leverage vs 5% in 2023); the long/short ratio stands at 3.6x. JPMorgan warns that rising semi stock volatility and elevated investor exposures create VaR-shock risk — a potential self-reinforcing selling loop. The sector's market cap-to-revenue ratio surpassed 6x, double that of Mag7. UBS's ML model warns that semis/tech hardware are 3-3.3 standard deviations overbought. At the same time, ~20% of hedge funds still have <10% AI exposure, sustaining the FOMO dynamic.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle accelerating: DRAM pricing +50-60% QoQ, MU responsible for 17% of S&P YTD gains
bullets.body: Samsung 2Q26 operating profit expected to exceed W100T as DRAM and NAND ASPs are tracking +50-60% QoQ versus an original forecast of +20-30%. Jefferies sees DRAM pricing growing 30% in 3Q26 and 40% in 4Q26. Citi raised its MU price target to $1,200, forecasting DRAM ASPs up 200% and NAND ASPs up 186% for full-year 2026. Multiple banks (GS, JPM, Citi, Jefferies) are modeling MU August-quarter EPS well above consensus ($28-30 vs street ~$20-23). MU is responsible for 17% of S&P 500 YTD gains. The sector faces crowded long positioning risk given MU has fallen on earnings 5 of the last 6 prints.

bullets.title: Accenture -25% on weak bookings signals AI is disrupting IT services, not enabling them yet
bullets.body: ACN's FQ3 miss — bookings -3% cc vs +7% consensus, FY26 guidance cut to 3-4% from 3-5%, and large managed services deals pushed into FY27 — is the most significant read on enterprise AI adoption in the digest period. The stock fell to 2017 lows. Multiple analysts warn of 'AI disintermediation' concerns: AI is replacing rather than augmenting consulting workflows, and CIOs plan to reduce spend with legacy software vendors in favor of AI-native solutions. ACN's $9B M&A pivot (including $4.175B for Dragos, runZero, NetRise in cybersecurity) is read as defensive.

bullets.title: Price Momentum vs. EPS Momentum at 97th percentile valuation gap — catch-up trade favored
bullets.body: 22V Research flags that NTM P/E premium of the top-decile Price Momentum basket vs. EPS Momentum basket reached the 97th percentile historically, driven by AI, Technology, and Industrials. EPS Momentum offers more attractive risk-reward. The AI theme is expected to broaden into chemicals and materials (NVIDIA Vera Rubin supply chain complexity). GARP basket gained 15.6% YTD; leading GARP industry groups include Banks, Insurance, Media, and Healthcare Equipment.

bullets.title: China economy weakening sharply: retail sales went negative, infrastructure investment collapsed
bullets.body: China's May retail sales declined 0.6% YoY — the first sub-zero print since 2022 — with 13 of 16 categories contracting. Infrastructure investment growth plunged to 0.6% YTD YoY in May from 4.3% in April. JPMorgan cut its China 2Q26 GDP forecast to 3.3% annualized. Consumer pessimism is rooted in labor market softening, not oil prices, and fiscal stimulus acceleration is seen as unlikely near-term. China's growth is increasingly concentrated in AI/tech exports, which account for roughly half of total export growth.

bullets.title: HDD pricing cycle extends through CY28+; WDC/STX FY28 EPS could be 70% above consensus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Asia trip produced upward revisions to WDC and STX HDD pricing checks. Vendors are targeting $25-30/TB pricing over 2-3 years versus the current <$15/TB. Demand is growing 40-50% annually while supply grows only 30-35%, with shortages expected through at least CY28. Hyperscalers are signing LTAs through 2032. WDC was up 32.6% and +333% YTD in the week; STX up similarly. MS raised WDC PT to $650 and STX to $1,035.

bullets.title: FOX acquires Roku for $160/share ($22B); FOXA -17%, 8 analyst downgrades on ROKU
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share (60% cash, 40% stock), creating a combined company with ~$24B revenue and ~$5B EBITDA growing ~8% CAGR. Combined entity becomes the third-largest US TV player by viewership. FOXA fell ~17% on dilution concerns while ROKU fell ~2%. Eight analysts downgraded ROKU to neutral/hold citing low competing bid probability. Deal expected to close H1 2027.

bullets.title: Global equity flows: HF gross leverage near highs but net selling in Info Tech and Semis
bullets.body: GS Prime Services reports that global equities were net sold for the first time in 5 weeks, driven by short sales outpacing long buys 1.3:1. Info Tech, Industrials, and Utilities were the most net sold sectors. Separately, HF gross leverage reached 98th percentile one-year readings while net leverage is at 94th percentile. Macro systematic strategies (Vol Target/CTA/Risk Parity) supplied ~$90B over the past month. Retail bought $27B in equities with single-name demand heavily tilted to TSLA, NVDA, and MU.

bullets.title: BoJ hiked to 1% (31-year high); ECB expects one more hike; BoE held but tightening bias intact
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bp to 1%, with next hike expected in October. The ECB is expected to deliver one more hike in September despite lower oil, as euro area core inflation remains sticky at ~2.5-2.6% through early 2027. The BoE held 7-2 but JPMorgan pushed its first expected BoE hike from July to November given UK CPI coming in at 2.8% vs 3.3% BoE forecast. Norges Bank signaled a September hike. This global central bank tightening synchrony adds cross-asset risk.

bullets.title: May retail sales beat (+0.9% m/m); consumer resilience holding despite energy shock
bullets.body: US May retail sales rose 0.9% m/m vs 0.5% consensus; the control group was up 0.7%. Morgan Stanley raised 2Q real consumption tracking to 2.9% q/q. Consumer confidence has rebounded ~10 points from early June lows on lower energy prices and rising stock market. CEO confidence correlates 72% with real GDP and is at its highest since 4Q24. Nominal personal income growing ~4% with real spending tracking ~2-3% reacceleration expected in H2.

bullets.title: Capital markets activity surging: M&A +64% YoY, IPOs +415%, equity issuance +117% in 2Q
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Deal Dashboard shows 2Q26 capital markets activity accelerating sharply: M&A annualized volume up 64% YoY QTD, equity issuance up 117% YoY led by North America at +234%, and IPOs up 415% YoY. Sponsor-backed M&A flipped positive to +1% YoY from -13% prior week. AI/data center debt financing reached $58B YTD (+71% YoY). This is a strong backdrop for investment bank earnings.

bullets.title: Enterprise AI adoption hitting cost and governance wall; 'tokenmaxxing' to 'token-minimizing'
bullets.body: Multiple data points this week confirm enterprise AI is shifting from experimentation to cost optimization. Uber exhausted its full 2026 AI budget in 4 months. Walmart, Microsoft, AT&T, and JPMorgan are all implementing usage caps or shifting to cheaper open-source models. AWS Bedrock AgentCore tasks were up 15x in 6 months but token rationalization is slowing broader enterprise adoption. AI spending is nonetheless expected to consume 6%+ of 2026 IT budgets vs 4.7% in 2H25.

bullets.title: China critical minerals remain key AI infrastructure chokepoint; no new US export controls since October
bullets.body: A special report finds China posts a $41B trade surplus in AI-related goods (power, batteries, optical networking — not chips) and accounts for ~28% of US AI-related imports when adjusting for rerouting through third countries. Critical minerals (gallium, germanium, indium phosphide) are gating factors for US data center buildout; China has extensive ability to tighten/loosen supply as leverage. Trump has imposed no new export controls on Chinese firms since October — a deliberate supply-chain truce. Trump included Coherent's CEO in his Beijing delegation specifically to lobby for indium phosphide access.

bullets.title: FERC approves Trump's AI data center grid acceleration plan; ERCOT batch process provides Aug clarity
bullets.body: FERC voted unanimously to approve Trump's plan directing grids to allow large data center loads to connect in a timely manner, and approved PJM's revised co-location tariff. Texas PUCT approved a batch interconnection methodology for ERCOT; 35GW of baseload and 65GW of load are under study in Batch 0, with results expected August 7. This is a structural positive for IPPs (VST, TLN, CEG) and behind-the-meter generation strategies. $130B in data center projects remain blocked or delayed due to public opposition.
